prize_parts.citation: for unifying electronic-structure theory and molecular dynamics, enabling first-principles simulation of the dynamics of molecules and materials

statement.case_for: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics is a single, original, sharply bounded methodological invention (1985) with a two-author credit trail that needs no trimming. It let nuclei move on electronic ground-state surfaces computed on the fly, which opened ab initio treatment of liquids, solids, interfaces and reactive chemistry such as bond breaking in solution, proton transfer and catalysis at surfaces. After four decades of independent use and extension it is fully mature, and it completes a line the Academy has already drawn through computational and theoretical chemistry (DFT in 1998, multiscale modelling in 2013). It is the only shortlisted candidate where the prize question reduces to one paper and two names.
statement.case_against: Opening support is thin: only four members ranked it, and my own first place is not matched by anyone else. Parrinello's wider body of work (metadynamics, machine-learned potentials) might make a citation built on the 1985 paper feel narrower than his full contribution, and a methods prize risks being seen as less topical than medicine-facing chemistry such as degraders or base editing. The computational lineage has also been recognised twice recently, so some colleagues may judge that area already served.

responses.point: Linke ranks targeted protein degradation first as a clear conceptual invention with a growing clinical pipeline, and also ranks Car-Parrinello second as fully mature and arguably overdue.
responses.response: I agree with the Car-Parrinello assessment and thank the chair for it, since it shows the case does not depend on my own field loyalty. On B037 I accept the concept is easy to state and widely reproduced. My reservation is that the opening ballots name at least five different trios (Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito among them), and no approved PROTAC exists. A prize that must exclude Sakamoto, Ciulli and Gray is harder to defend than one with two names that nobody disputes. If the committee wants degraders I would like the molecular-glue and PROTAC halves argued separately before we fix three names.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks Buchwald-Hartwig first and Car-Parrinello third, calling the latter a clean two-person discovery, long overdue, and a good fit with the 2013 and 1998 simulation and DFT prizes.
responses.response: I largely share his reading and note that he and I agree on both B005 and B016, differing only in order. Where I qualify him is the claim that B005 is overdue rather than constrained: C-N coupling is a superb method, but it extends the logic of the 2010 prize to another bond type, whereas Car-Parrinello opened a new capability (ab initio dynamics) that had no predecessor. I would still happily support B005 as an alternative, and I would not fight a Buchwald-Hartwig prize if the committee prefers synthetic chemistry this year.

responses.point: Somfai ranks PROTAC/glue degraders first and Buchwald-Hartwig second, stressing that degraders reach once-undruggable targets and are in late-stage trials, with a three-person configuration that is a plausible judgement call.
responses.response: The undruggable-target argument is scientifically real, but it is a statement about impact, and clinical proof of an approved degrader is still pending, which Somfai himself flags. I do not think that impact should outrank maturity and clean attribution when we are choosing among shortlisted candidates. I agree with his handling of B005, where he and I both exclude Kosugi from a two-person prize to keep the focus on the decisive generalisation.

responses.point: Aili ranks genetic code expansion first, as a foundational engineering platform for non-canonical amino acids, with Schultz, Chin and Yokoyama as the central names.
responses.response: I rank B002 third and agree it is mature and broadly adopted. Our difference is attribution: Aili credits Yokoyama while I and several others credit Wang as the key early experimentalist alongside Schultz, and Mehl is a fifth plausible name. That is a real split inside one candidate, which makes B002 harder to settle than B016. I would want the committee to resolve whether the foundational step is the E. coli and eukaryotic orthogonal pair (Schultz, Wang) or the later multi-codon and ribosome work (Chin) before it becomes a front-runner.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing first, as a genuine chemical-biology invention built on molecular design, preferring Liu alone because the foundational CRISPR credit was already awarded in 2020.
responses.response: Liu alone is the cleanest base-editing configuration and I find the argument for it persuasive, and my own view is that the invention is clearly Liu's. My doubt is timing: the CRISPR prize in 2020 and the first-in-human therapies still maturing make this a strong case for the near future rather than the most pressing one now. I would place it above PROTACs on attribution cleanliness, but below the methods that already have four decades of confirmation.

uncertainties: Whether the committee would rather split the prize, for example B016 with a single-name second part such as B060 (Liu), which fits the three-person limit, or keep a single clean achievement.
Whether recent prizes for DFT (1998) and multiscale modelling (2013) make another computational-methods award less likely to win a majority, however strong the science.
Whether Parrinello's later methodological work should be mentioned in the citation or deliberately left out so the prize stays tied to the 1985 invention.
I have not independently checked citation or usage figures for any candidate and am relying on the ballots and the shortlist.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate: my postdoctoral EVB collaboration was with Arieh Warshel, who is not credited on any shortlisted ballot. I do work in the same broad area of molecular simulation as B016 and have used related methods, which I note openly as a subject-closeness point rather than a personal tie to Car or Parrinello.
